title: Simon Willison traces three LLM inflection points in twelve months
summary: Simon Willison&\#x27;s retrospective, published on the one-year anniversary of Claude Opus 4.5, argues that LLM and coding-agent capability crossed three inflection points in twelve months. He credits Claude Opus 4.5 and OpenAI&\#x27;s GPT-5.1 family \(Instant, Thinking, GPT-5.1-Codex and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max\) with making coding agents reliably useful for his daily work in late 2025, then Claude Fable 5 in June 2026 with defining "Fable class" models that can pursue a defined goal with tools, a group he extends to Fable 5/5.1/5.2, Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra and possibly Gemini 4 Neon. He identifies a third inflection in September–October 2026, when frontier models became notably better at 3D modeling and game development, citing Opus 5.5&\#x27;s response to a request to make a game "a LOT more fun" after 12 hours of playtesting. These are the author&\#x27;s experience-based judgments rather than independent benchmarks, and the supplied post cuts off before his discussion of Fable 5.2.
